name: Sagebrush shrubland
notes: Grey-green big sagebrush 1-2 m dominates with bunchgrasses between shrubs; pinyon and juniper only on slopes; Great Basin and Columbia Plateau of the western USA.

canopy.name: Utah juniper
canopy.source: Juniperus osteosperma, Great Basin/Colorado Plateau, shrubby conifer 3-8 m on rocky slopes — USDA PLANTS

canopy.name: Singleleaf pinyon
canopy.source: Pinus monophylla, Great Basin pinyon-juniper woodland, 5-12 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Big sagebrush
shrub.source: Artemisia tridentata, dominant Great Basin shrub, grey-green aromatic 0.6-2.5 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Rubber rabbitbrush
shrub.source: Ericameria nauseosa, western N America sagebrush steppe, yellow autumn flowers, 0.6-2 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Antelope bitterbrush
shrub.source: Purshia tridentata, Great Basin and intermountain west, browse shrub 0.6-3 m, cream flowers — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Shadscale
shrub.source: Atriplex confertifolia, Great Basin saline valley floors, spiny grey shrub 0.3-1 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Greasewood
shrub.source: Sarcobatus vermiculatus, alkaline basins of western N America, 1-2.5 m — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Bluebunch wheatgrass
ground.source: Pseudoroegneria spicata, dominant bunchgrass of the sagebrush steppe, 0.4-1 m — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Idaho fescue
ground.source: Festuca idahoensis, intermountain west bunchgrass, blue-green, 30-60 cm — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Indian ricegrass
ground.source: Achnatherum hymenoides, western N American sandy soils, airy bunchgrass 30-60 cm — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Arrowleaf balsamroot
ground.source: Balsamorhiza sagittata, sagebrush steppe forb with yellow sunflower heads, 20-60 cm — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Sandberg bluegrass
ground.source: Poa secunda, small early-season bunchgrass throughout the sagebrush steppe, 10-40 cm — USDA PLANTS
